entries.description: AnyPS5 — утилита, автоматически преобразующая исполняемые файлы PlayStation 5 в нативные форматы Linux и Windows. В основе проекта лежит relinker, который переписывает бинарный код и подключает реализованные системные PRX‑библиотеки, позволяя запускать игры без эмуляции или отдельного рантайма. Сборка relinker‑only работает на macOS, включая Apple Silicon, а веб‑конвертер обеспечивает локальное преобразование файлов в браузере. Поддерживается ввод через SDL‑совместимые контроллеры, клавиатуру и мышь, а прогресс по поддержке функций и шейдеров отображается в онлайн‑дашбордах. Проект ориентирован на исследователей, архивистов и разработчиков, желающих изучать или сохранять PS5‑контент, при условии наличия легально полученных бинарных образов.

# About

Tool for automatic executables porting to Linux and Windows.

The relinker-only build runs on macOS, including Apple silicon.

[**Web converter**](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/) - files stay on your device.

![anyps5_collage1](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed2f0b2d-33d3-46d7-ab88-767ca872fc99)

Includes a [relinker](core/relinker) that converts executable to the target system's native format and implementations of [system prx libraries](core/libs/prx) suitable for dynamic linking. No emulation or separate runtime process.

[**Discord**](https://discord.gg/BHFztBPUe), [Usage](docs/user/USAGE.md), [Build instructions](docs/dev/BUILD.md), [Architecture](docs/dev/ARCHITECTURE.md), [Technical debt of the project](docs/dev/TechnicalDebt.md), [code style conventions](docs/dev/CONVENTIONS.md), [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)

## Status

[![libraries](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/badge-libraries.svg)](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/progress.html) [![shaders](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/badge-shaders.svg)](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/progress.html)

[![progress map](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/progress.svg)](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/progress.html)

[Progress history](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/history.html)

<sub>* System libraries: percentage of the functions known to the project so far (declared in [core/libs/prx](core/libs/prx)), not of every PS5 system function. The total grows as more functions are declared.</sub>

Unsupported or unexpected states strictly throw `std::runtime_error`. `what()` is printed to stderr and the process terminates.

The [shader recompiler](core/shader/recompiler/Recompiler.cpp) successfully produces SPIR-V (validated via [Spirv-Tools](3rdparty/SPIRV-Tools) when built with `ANYPS5_ENABLE_SPIRV_TOOLS`).

## Compatibility

Per-game progress (stage reached, open blockers, libraries and GPU coverage) is tracked on the [blocker map](https://alxcbtw.github.io/anyps5-roadmap/), a community project built from public GitHub data ([source](https://github.com/AlxcBTW/anyps5-roadmap)). Test reports go in the [Game bring-up](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/discussions/categories/game-bring-up) discussions, one thread per title.

## Input mapping

SDL-mapped game controllers are supported, including analog sticks and triggers. Keyboard and mouse controls can be configured with an `anyps5-input.ini` file. See [input mapping](docs/user/INPUT_MAPPING.md) for the supported devices and configuration format.

## Disclaimer

This project is intended for interoperability, research, preservation, and compatibility purposes. It does not include, distribute, or require copyrighted software, firmware, cryptographic keys, or proprietary libraries. Users are responsible for ensuring that any binaries used with this project are obtained and used in accordance with applicable laws and their respective license terms.

latest.readme_excerpt: # Ghidra Software Reverse Engineering Framework Ghidra is a software reverse engineering (SRE) framework created and maintained by the [National Security Agency][nsa] Research Directorate. This framework includes a suite of full-featured, high-end software analysis tools that enable users to analyze compiled code on a variety of platforms including Windows, macOS, and Linux. Capabilities include disassembly, assembly, decompilation, graphing, and scripting, along with hundreds of other features. Ghidra supports a wide variety of processor instruction sets and executable formats and can be run in both user-interactive and automated modes. Users may also develop their own Ghidra extension components and/or scripts using Java or Python. In support of NSA's Cybersecurity mission, Ghidra was built to solve scaling and teaming problems on complex SRE efforts, and to provide a customizable and extensible SRE research platform. NSA has applied Ghidra SRE capabilities to a variety of problems that involve analyzing malicious code and generating deep insights for SRE analysts who seek a better understanding of potential vulnerabilities in networks and systems. # Claude Code Plugins Directory

A curated directory of high-quality plugins for Claude Code.

> **⚠️ Important:** Make sure you trust a plugin before installing, updating, or using it. Anthropic does not control what MCP servers, files, or other software are included in plugins and cannot verify that they will work as intended or that they won't change. See each plugin's homepage for more information.

## Structure

- **`/plugins`** - Internal plugins developed and maintained by Anthropic
- **`/external_plugins`** - Third-party plugins from partners and the community

## Installation

Plugins can be installed directly from this marketplace via Claude Code's plugin system.

To install, run `/plugin install {plugin-name}@claude-plugins-official`

or browse for the plugin in `/plugin > Discover`

## Contributing

### Internal Plugins

Internal plugins are developed by Anthropic team members. See `/plugins/example-plugin` for a reference implementation.

### External Plugins

Third-party partners can submit plugins for inclusion in the marketplace. External plugins must meet quality and security standards for approval. To submit a new plugin, use the [plugin directory submission form](https://clau.de/plugin-directory-submission).

## Plugin Structure

Each plugin follows a standard structure:

```
plugin-name/
├── .claude-plugin/
│   └── plugin.json      # Plugin metadata (required)
├── .mcp.json            # MCP server configuration (optional)
├── commands/            # Slash commands (optional)
├── agents/              # Agent definitions (optional)
├── skills/              # Skill definitions (optional)
└── README.md            # Documentation
```

## Plugin names are immutable

The `name` field in a marketplace entry is an **immutable slug**. Once a plugin has been published, its `name` must not change — users have it installed under that slug, and renaming it breaks their install with a `plugin-not-found` error.

- To change how a plugin is labeled in the UI, set or update `displayName` instead.
- If a rename is genuinely unavoidable, add an entry to the top-level `renames` map in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` so existing installs auto-migrate:

```json
"renames": {
  "old-name": "new-name"
}
```

The Claude Code plugin loader reads this map and transparently rewrites the old slug to the new one on the user's next sync.

## Skill-bundle plugins

When a plugin's source repository ships skills (`SKILL.md` files) without a `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` manifest, the marketplace entry can declare the skills directly using `strict: false` and an explicit `skills` array.

```json
{
  "name": "example-bundle",
  "description": "Brief description of the bundled skills.",
  "author": { "name": "Author Name" },
  "category": "development",
  "source": {
    "source": "git-subdir",
    "url": "https://github.com/example-org/sdk.git",
    "path": "packages/agent-skills",
    "ref": "main",
    "sha": "<commit sha>"
  },
  "strict": false,
  "skills": [
    "./skill-a",
    "./skill-b",
    "./skill-c"
  ],
  "homepage": "https://github.com/example-org/sdk"
}
```

Each path in `skills` is relative to `source.path` and points at a directory containing a `SKILL.md`. Paths can reach deeper than a single level — for example, `["./libA/skill-1", "./libB/skill-2"]` exposes a curated subset across multiple library subdirectories. Each skill is registered as `<plugin-name>:<skill-name>` in Claude Code.

For the underlying schema, see [Strict mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces) in the marketplace documentation.

## License

Please see each linked plugin for the relevant LICENSE file.

## Documentation

For more information on developing Claude Code plugins, see the [official documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins).

Quit Claude Code mid-task, > start OpenAI Codex in the same directory, continue without > re-explaining the architecture, the failed approaches, or the open > questions. **Website: [aimemory.sh](https://aimemory.sh)** [![Website](https://img.shields.io/badge/website-aimemory.sh-blue)](https://aimemory.sh) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/akitaonrails/ai-memory)](https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory/releases/latest) [![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.95+-blue)](rust-toolchain.toml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) ## Why ai-memory Your coding agent probably has a memory feature already. Claude Code takes its own notes, Cursor remembers some things, and every platform is adding more. They all have the same limits: the notes live on one machine, belong to one agent, and drop out of view when you switch tools or hand the work to a teammate. ai-memory removes those limits. - **It follows you across agents.** More than twenty harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Grok, Devin, Kimi, Kiro, and others) feed one shared memory. Quit Claude Code mid-task, open Codex in the same directory, and the next agent picks up a handoff that says where you left off, what failed, and what is still open. Handoffs are a typed protocol: each one has an owner and is claimed exactly once. - **It can carry the session, not just a summary.** Start agents with `ai-memory run`: quit Claude Code, run `ai-memory run codex`, and Codex gets the shared workstream plus a private, temporary local projection of Claude's visible native history for exact details the bounded startup packet omitted. The remote server receives only the harness and session identity, never the local transcript path or body. Direct harness launches behave exactly as before. - **It follows you across projects.** A small profile of how you usually work (your package manager, test layout, architecture habits) reaches every new repository at session start, so you stop re-explaining yourself. It sits below each repository's rules file as a default. It is on by default for a single user, and on a shared server it is opt-in and private per person. See [`docs/cross-project-profile.md`](docs/cross-project-profile.md). - **It follows you across machines.** Memory lives in a server you run, on the same laptop, a homelab box, or anywhere else, so the project you left on the desktop is the project you resume on the laptop, with the same knowledge and the same open questions. - **It works for a team.** Point everyone at one server, and what one person's sessions learn, everyone's agents can retrieve. Knowledge is shared per project; personal handoffs stay personal. Multi-user auth, per-person attribution, and an audit log are built in and are not a paid tier. - **Your memory is plain markdown.** The source of truth is a git-backed wiki of ordinary `.md` files: `grep` it, open it in Obsidian, edit it by hand, `rsync` it. The database is a derived index that can always be rebuilt from the files. There is no vector store to maintain and no content locked in a binary blob. - **It captures the work itself, silently.** Lifecycle hooks record what happened (prompts, tool calls, session boundaries), sanitize it at a typed privacy boundary before anything is stored, and the server consolidates it into readable pages. You do not have to ask it to remember anything. The default path uses **zero LLM calls**: capture, search, and handoffs all work with no API key. - **It ages memory without an LLM.** Memory decays on a schedule you can tune per tier, and memory you use decays *slower*: opening a page, searching it, or reaching it through a link counts as use. When episodic notes go cold they can be compacted down to their durable facts (file paths, error codes, decisions) instead of dropped. Near-duplicates collapse into one, and likely contradictions get flagged, all with **zero API calls**. # Marble Skill Taxonomy

An open, structured taxonomy of **what children learn** across the primary/elementary years — decomposed into fine-grained "micro-topics", wired into a prerequisite graph, and aligned to national curriculum standards. Produced by [Marble](https://withmarble.com).

> **Version:** `v1` · **Topics:** 1,591 · **Prerequisite edges:** 3,225 · **Subjects:** 8

## See it

![The taxonomy as a rotating 3D graph: every dot a micro-topic, colored by subject, wired by prerequisites](media/curriculum-viz.gif)

Every dot is a micro-topic, colored by subject; height is age; each thread is a prerequisite ([full-quality video](media/curriculum-viz.mp4)). Explore it interactively at [withmarble.com/curriculum](https://withmarble.com/curriculum) — tap any concept to trace everything a learner must master before it.


## What this is

Most curriculum data is either a flat list of standards or locked inside a product. This dataset is a **connected graph of learning**:

- **1,591 micro-topics** — a single, teachable idea (e.g. *"Building sentences"*, *"Apparent brightness of stars"*), each with a plain-language description, mastery **evidence** criteria, a type (conceptual / procedural / representational / language / meta), a subject + domain, and an approximate age range.
- **3,225 prerequisite dependencies** — a directed acyclic graph: *"topic X depends on prerequisite Y"*, each edge tagged `hard`/`soft` and carrying a one-line **reason**.
- **Curriculum alignment** — each micro-topic links to the standards it was distilled from (NGSS, Common Core, the UK National Curriculum, and more).
- **Teaching research** — 1,051 records covering the current Science and Mathematics topics: teaching approaches, concrete learning activities, feedback, assessment guidance and linked sources. Coverage is partial; the other 540 topics have no research in this release.
- **Domain clusters** — 176 parent-friendly one-paragraph summaries per (subject, domain, age band).

### Subjects

| Subject | Topics |
|---|---:|
| Science | 547 |
| Mathematics | 504 |
| English | 286 |
| History | 90 |
| Personal & Social Development | 88 |
| Life Skills | 37 |
| Computing | 21 |
| Learning to Learn | 18 |

## Files

All data lives in [`data/`](data/) as UTF-8 JSON. See [`schema/`](schema/) for JSON Schemas and [`manifest.json`](data/manifest.json) for counts + SHA-256 checksums.

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| [`data/topics.json`](data/topics.json) | The micro-topics (graph **nodes**). |
| [`data/dependencies.json`](data/dependencies.json) | Prerequisite **edges** (`topicId` depends on `prerequisiteId`). |
| [`data/curriculum-standards.json`](data/curriculum-standards.json) | The source curriculum standards, grouped by curriculum. |
| [`data/clusters.json`](data/clusters.json) | Parent-friendly domain summaries. |
| [`data/teaching-research.json`](data/teaching-research.json) | Teaching research joined by `topicId`, with explicit coverage and publication notes (~24 MB). |
| [`data/manifest.json`](data/manifest.json) | Counts, per-subject breakdown, per-file checksums. |

### A topic

```json
{
  "id": "mt_N8CpN1EJrP",
  "type": "CONCEPTUAL",
  "subject": "English",
  "domain": "Grammar & Punctuation",
  "name": "Building sentences",
  "description": "Understand that words combine to make sentences — a sentence expresses a complete thought…",
  "ageRangeStart": 4,
  "ageRangeEnd": 6,
  "centrality": 0.257,
  "evidence": [
    "Distinguish between complete sentences and fragments",
    "Compose a complete sentence with a subject and verb"
  ],
  "assessmentPrompt": "If {{name}} says something like \"The dog\", can they tell you that's not a complete sentence…?",
  "standards": ["ccss-ela:L.K.1f", "uk-nc-2013:Eng.App2.Y1.Sent.1"]
}
```

- `id` — stable identifier (`mt_…`), referenced by dependencies and by neighbours.
- `standards` — keys into `curriculum-standards.json` (`"<curriculum-slug>:<code>"`).
- `assessmentPrompt` — a natural-language check for the idea. Contains a `{{name}}` placeholder (the child's name); substitute or strip before display.

### A dependency

```json
{ "topicId": "mt__00ZSLnB7p", "prerequisiteId": "mt_VBl1T1sFCM", "strength": "hard",
  "reason": "Must understand vibrations make sound before finding volume patterns" }
```

`topicId` **depends on** `prerequisiteId`. Reverse the edge to get "unlocks".

## Teaching research

[`data/teaching-research.json`](data/teaching-research.json) adds **how a topic
might be taught** to the graph of what children learn. It covers **547 Science**
and **504 Mathematics** topics. `coverage.missingTopicIds` and per-subject counts
make the **540 topics without research** explicit; absence is not a judgement
about whether a topic can be taught.

The file has `schemaVersion: 1` and taxonomy `version: "v1"`. Each `records[]`
entry joins `topics.json` through `topicId` and contains:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pedagogy` | Original teaching summary, practices, representation

# D2R Mobile **An open-source iOS / macOS compatibility layer for Diablo II: Resurrected with the Reign of the Warlock expansion.** It brings the Nintendo Switch release you bought, expansion included, to iPhone, iPad and Mac in full: the original game code runs natively, every control is rebuilt for touch, the frame rate holds at 60 fps, and you are in a game one second after the main menu. There is now a native macOS version as well (first version): on an Apple silicon Mac it starts on double-click and works with keyboard, mouse and gamepad. Apple TV 4K (3rd generation, A15) has a community port (developer preview) that has reached the character-selection screen only on its author's device; see the device table below. This is not a tech demo that "sort of runs". It is a mobile version polished for daily play, from your first character all the way through the endgame. Platforms: iPhone / iPad (iOS 26 and later; iOS 18 – 25 with the older-API build) · Mac (Apple silicon, macOS 26 or later; macOS 15 – 25 with the older-API build) · Apple TV 4K (3rd generation, A15; community port, developer preview) · Game version: Switch release with Reign of the Warlock, 1.0.34.0 (corresponds to PC version 3.3.94012) · English / 中文 / Español · License: MIT · **Bring your own game files** 中文: [README.zh-CN.md](README.zh-CN.md) · Español: [README.es.md](README.es.md)

| 100% | 60 fps | about 1 s | about 3.8 W | |:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | The original gameplay, because it is the original program | Steady, with no drops once the device warms up | From the main menu into a game | Whole-device power draw at 60 fps | ## What it is, and what it is not **It is:** - The game's own aarch64 program, **executing directly on the device**, with no emulated CPU. iPhone and Switch use the same class of processor; only the handful of instructions that cannot run unchanged under Apple's kernel are rewritten, and every other byte of the program is left exactly as shipped. Every class, every Runeword, Terror Zones, bosses, drop rules and quest flow are identical to the original. - The platform services the game expects — system calls, the file system, the graphics API, audio, input — provided by a small host written for Apple platforms. The graphics API is reimplemented entirely on Apple's Metal with no emulation layer in between, and the shaders are translated offline from the game's originals. - A port built for phones, and taken all the way: a complete touch control scheme, edge-to-edge iPhone and true full-screen iPad display, controller support, a power saver mode, save sync, English and Chinese, and a whole set of endgame modes and quality-of-life features the original never had. **It is not:** - An emulator, cloud gaming, or streaming. - **A source of game content. It contains none and distributes none.** There is no game program, art, text, data table or shader in this repository; all of that is generated on your own machine from your own files (see [docs/GAME_FILES.md](docs/GAME_FILES.md)). What the repository does carry is the interface information we recorded to make the port work — shader interface descriptions, the graphics API function table, addresses inside the program and the like — listed item by item in [docs/DERIVED.md](docs/DERIVED.md). - Online. There is no multiplayer; the game runs fully offline and needs no online account. ## Battle-tested All **44** iPhones and iPads in the closed beta — 35 devices registered for direct install (25 iPhones and 10 iPads), plus 9 TestFlight accounts with one device each — **completed Normal, Nightmare and Hell with multiple characters**, and the experience was excellent. From an iPhone 14 Pro Max with 6 GB of memory to the latest iPad Pro, not one device fell behind. | | Models | |---|---| | iPhone | 14 Pro Max, 15, 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max, 16 Plus, 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max, 17 Pro Max and more | | iPad | iPad Air, iPad mini, iPad Pro 11-inch and 12.9 / 13-inch (including M2 and M4) and more | | Lowest model tested | **iPhone 14 Pro Max (A16, 6 GB): a flawless 60 fps** | iPhone and iPad share a single install package.

Git designed for AI agents.

Anthropic built **Scion**, a faster version control system for coding agents, and described it in [Redesigning source control](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/redesigning-source-control): a server-centric system built for hundreds of agents that read, write and land code at the same time. Scion is internal to Anthropic and is not available to the public. So I built **gitai**: an open-source version of that design that anyone can run, and that the community can improve and maintain together. MIT licensed. Vendor neutral: the server never calls a language model, and every AI feature works with any provider, or none. gitai is an independent implementation of the publicly described design. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic. --- ## Why Classic Git hosting was built for humans who clone a repository, work for hours and push once. Coding agents work differently: thousands of short-lived tasks, each touching a few files, each wanting to land in seconds, all on the same branches. Full clones, merge queues and client-side history walks become the bottleneck. Scion's answer is to move the work to the server: clients stay online and fetch only what they need, history questions are answered (and cached) by the server, changes land through a compare-and-swap instead of a queue, every update is an entry in a changeset log, and the repository state lives in a consistent database plus object storage so servers scale out. gitai implements these ideas, with normal Git repositories underneath. ## The Scion ideas, implemented | Scion idea | In gitai | |---|---| | **Always-online clients** that fetch exactly what they need | `ObjectService` serves single objects and sparse trees; `graft clone` and `graft sparse` materialize only the paths you ask for. | | **Source control as an API**: history runs on the server | Blame, path history, ancestry and code search run server-side and are memoized as derived data, computed once per commit. | | **Landing without a merge queue** | `UserLand` rebases a change onto the current tip and lands it with a compare-and-swap; concurrent lands on one branch are batched into a single reference update. | | **Automatic conflict resolution** | A conflicting land is resolved by a resolver you choose (any LLM provider, a deterministic tool, or none) through a versioned, vendor-neutral protocol. | | **Changeset log** | Every accepted reference update is recorded with its operation and actor in a dense, ordered log that clients list or watch live. | | **Storage core: a database and object storage, stateless servers** | Each change is a changeset in a write-ahead log in SQLite or PostgreSQL, with a compare-and-swap per reference; packs live in object storage (file, S3, GCS, Azure). Server nodes are caches that any node can rebuild, so you add nodes to scale. | | **Test after landing, revert the culprit** | `graft-verify` tests the tip, bisects a failure and reverts the change that broke it. | | **Monitoring agents ("superfans")** | Agents follow the changeset stream and report what matters to each component, also through Slack. | | **Agent-friendly review** | Reviews with semantic approval rules: a comment-only change can need fewer approvals than a logic change. | | **Agents as first-class users** | Per-agent tokens, an RPC allowlist and branch policies decide what each agent may do. | | **Strict cache tiers** | `graft-cache` caches immutable objects in daemon and regional tiers, verifying every object. | ## Architecture ``` agents, CI jobs, sparse workspaces graft CLI / Go SDK | v gRPC +-------------------------------------------------+ | graft-cache (optional daemon and cache tiers) | +------------------------+------------------------+ v +---------------------------------------------------------------+ | gitai server (any number of nodes) | | land - objects - changesets - derived data - search - review | | write path: changeset + compare-and-swap per reference | +-----------+--------------------------------+------------------+ |

latest.readme_excerpt: # BRUTAL Framework **A free, open source C# framework for making games, or your own game engine.** BRUTAL is a framework. You can make a game directly with it, or use it as the foundation for a separate engine. We made Kitten Space Agency directly on BRUTAL. Ludeon built their Waylith engine on it to move RimWorld off Unity. At its core is a custom interop layer giving C# direct access to native APIs and libraries. Around that we've built mathematics, memory management, strings, collections, job scheduling, logging, localization, and bindings for Vulkan, GLFW, Dear ImGui, FMOD, RakNet, Jolt and Box2D. BRUTAL doesn't make the architectural decisions for you. You write your own stack. You can use whatever NuGet packages you want, including third-party ones. It's called BRUTAL for a reason. In some ways it's much harder to use than Unity, Unreal or Godot. In other ways, particularly if you're doing something unusual, it's considerably easier. You actually have to know what you want to do first. ## Why You are only as independent as your tools are. Developers have surrendered an extraordinary amount of control over their work to companies whose interests are not necessarily aligned with their own. We're not suggesting everyone should make their own game engine. We're suggesting every developer should have the option to, without having to spend four years building the foundations first. What that means in practice: - **Free, including for commercial games.** No royalties. We don't want a percentage of your game's revenue. We ask for credit. - **Open source.** The source is here under an MIT-based licence. If one day we stop being accountable to developers, you can fork it and go your own way. - **Deliberately small.** We do a few low-level things well: interop, memory, concurrency, maths, strings, and bindings to native libraries, on the latest C# and Vulkan. We avoid allocations and unnecessary overhead and use unmanaged memory and unsafe code where it makes sense. - **A foundation, like a kernel.** Think of the Linux kernel and something like Ubuntu. It's not an exact comparison, but it gets the idea across. We provide the foundation and you build your own systems on top. ### What BRUTAL is not BRUTAL is not trying to be a general-purpose engine. There is no editor, no scene graph and no renderer, and we're not adding them. We push back on efforts to add more, because adding everything is how the industry ended up with the kind of engines we don't want to use. # Handwired

Turn your regular JavaScript code into a neural net; no training, exact, yet also fully differentiable!

## How It Works

A program's made of if-else, loops, and state. Handwired transforms them into matrix multiplication + reglu over floats. For example:

```ts
const a = 5
const result = (a > 4) ? 10 : 12
```

The above can be expressed as basic arithmetic:

```ts
const a = 5
// Math.max(0, x) is ReLU. For an integer a, above4 is 1 if a > 4, and 0 otherwise
const above4 = Math.max(0, a - 4) - Math.max(0, a - 5)
// Both branches compute, and above4 picks one
const result = above4 * 10 + (1 - above4) * 12
```

You can calculate that by hand and see that both arrive at the same result.

We then collect the + and * and relu into a giant matmul, and either run it on JS or WebGPU, for fun.

Because we basically only use these 2 primitives:
- the full program stays differentiable
- the weights don't need training since they're written manually
- existing gpu techniques, such as fusion, sparsity, reordering, have a great time optimizing such minimal primitives

This unlocks lots of funny use-cases, like:
- unfreezing the weights and train them (what does that even do? Let's find out!)
- attaching a specific frozen program to a generic neural net and train end-to-end (now a nanoGPT can do both Shakespeare and your particular UI?)
- achieving GPU-level of parallelism with JS code that was written in a traditional single-threaded way (see the JSON search demo that runs in milliseconds over 100k documents)

## Play With It

Try the demos live: https://chenglou.me/handwired/

`git clone && bun install`, then `bun start` to run them locally. Check `docs/`, `src/` and `template/` to get started! (`lab/` is a bunch of old experiments you can check or ignore)

Play your own copy of **The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom** natively on Apple silicon Mac, iPhone, and iPad. Bring your game file (XCI or NSP) and your `prod.keys`; one script builds a Mac app or an unsigned iPhone/iPad IPA. The iOS build requires iOS/iPadOS 26 and iPhone 14 or newer. It is not an emulator: the game's own ARM64 code runs directly on Apple chips (rewritten where the operating system requires it), the Switch system services are answered by a small host, and the game's NVN graphics are rebuilt on Metal. Nothing from the game is in this repository, and the project is not affiliated with Nintendo. Version 1.4.3 has been played on an iPhone 14 and an iPad; see [iPhone and iPad](#iphone-and-ipad).

> [!TIP]
> **Every shader in the shared list is ready before you play.** On a Mac the game does not stop to compile it, and on an iPhone or iPad nothing is missing from the picture. The more places players cover, the smoother the game gets for everyone.

# Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection for Windows

**Uncharted 1, 2 and 3 from the PS4 collection running natively on Windows 10 and 11, by [SuperMedo](https://github.com/Supermedo).** Mohammed Albarghouthi

Same idea as my [Bloodborne port](https://github.com/Supermedo/bloodborne_pc): the original PS4 game
code runs directly on your PC and the graphics are translated to Vulkan. Unpack the zip, start
`Uncharted.exe`, pick your game folder, choose a game and press **PLAY**.

**[Download the latest version](https://github.com/Supermedo/uncharted_pc/releases/latest)** · **[Join the Discord](https://discord.gg/s3RgH6cRfJ)**

> **No game files are included.** You need your own decrypted dump of the collection
> (CUSA02343, CUSA02320, ...: the folder with eboot.bin, big2-ps4_Shipping.elf,
> big3-ps4_Shipping.elf, sce_sys, u1data, u2data and u3data).
> This project is not affiliated with Sony Interactive Entertainment or Naughty Dog.

## Features

- All three games from one launcher: Drake's Fortune, Among Thieves and Drake's Deception.
- 60 FPS like on PS4, or 120 FPS (higher rates are experimental).
- Anti-aliasing with TAA, AMD FSR 3.1, AMD FSR 4 or NVIDIA DLSS (DLAA).
- Frame generation: AMD FSR 3 (any GPU) or NVIDIA DLSS (RTX 40 2x, RTX 50 up to 4x).
- Keyboard, mouse and controller together, all remappable. Mouse look in U3.
- Add to Steam and desktop shortcuts from the launcher, automatic updates.

## Requirements

- Windows 10 (1903 or later) or Windows 11, 64-bit.
- An Intel Core 4th generation (Haswell) or newer, an AMD Ryzen, or an AMD FX.
- A graphics card with Vulkan 1.3 and a current driver, with **6 GB of video memory or more**.
  4 GB cards (GTX 1650, RX 570) run out of video memory and crash after a while; on those, keep
  Anti-aliasing and Frame generation off.
- About 8 GB of free memory (RAM + page file).

## Known problems

- **Uncharted 3, Cartagena square (chapter 2):** at high frame rates (240 Hz setting, ~80 FPS)
  the game could freeze and close with "GPU crash: the graphics device was lost". It came from
  the speed fix for that area and is fixed in 0.3. If it still happens to you, set Frame rate to
  60 on the Display page and open an issue with your `user\last_run.log`.
- **Uncharted 3:** green or black shapes flash for a single frame on some characters (Sully's
  shirt in Cartagena). It happens in shadPS4 too, so it's a shader translation problem. Not fixed yet.
- **Crash with "ASSERTION: GetRenderFrameParams(frameToFreeInstancesFor)->m_gfxEopTick"**
  (mostly U1 after the first cutscene): the game expected the GPU side to be done with a frame it
  wanted to reuse, and stopped when it wasn't yet (shaders building on a first run). Fixed in
  0.3.2 (0.3.4 for the 1.02 versions): the game now waits for it. If you still see it, open an
  issue with your log.
- **Intel HD / UHD graphics:** a black screen on the HD 630 is fixed in 0.3.3. Older Intel chips
  (HD 520) can still crash inside Intel's own driver.
- **Uncharted 3 London bar crash** (fault at `0xd9c59b`, or device lost in the bar fight): fixed in
  0.3.4.
- **Uncharted 2 loading crashes** (`ReadSync file (req/read: ...)`, white textures then
  `iSubMesh < m_numSubMeshInstances`): file reads could come back cut short. Fixed in 0.3.5.
- **Older CPUs:** the games use instructions of the PS4's processor (AVX, BMI1, MOVBE, LZCNT).
  AMD FX runs since 0.3.6 (its missing MOVBE is emulated, a bit slower). Intel Core 3rd generation
  and older can't run the games yet; the game says so instead of crashing with 0xc000001d.
- **Uncharted 2, train wreck:** `IsFinite(deltaTransform)` in character-leg-ik.cpp, fixed in 0.3.6
  for the EU 1.00 version.
- Frame rates above 120 are experimental.

## Building

MSYS2 CLANG64 on Windows: `bash build.sh` builds `out\bb-probe.exe`, and
`bash packaging/windows/package.sh` makes `dist\uncharted-windows` and the zip.

## Credits

Built on [bbport](https://github.com/deadinside28/bloodborne_pc), the native Linux port of
Bloodborne by deadinside28, and on the [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4)
renderer. Video decoding (Videodec2) and the DLSS bridge come from
[IFreemz/shadPS4-Bloodborne-DLSS-FSR](https://github.com/IFreemz/shadPS4-Bloodborne-DLSS-FSR).
Thanks to Mindro for the shadPS4 Uncharted build that showed which problems to look for.

Also used: [FSR-Vulkan](https://github.com/FireBurn/FSR-Vulkan) and the AMD FidelityFX SDK (FSR),

[sirit](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/sirit), [magic_enum](https://github.com/Neargye/magic_enum),
[xbyak](https://github.com/herumi/xbyak),
[Vulkan Memory Allocator](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/VulkanM

# earshot

**Ears for coding agents.**

<!-- launch video -->
[**Watch the 22 s launch film**](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/earshot/releases/tag/v0.1.0) - every sound in it was made
in code by `earshot forge`; no recordings, no music track.

![Frames from the launch film](docs/media/launch_frames.png)

AI coding agents can now write the code that renders a film, a product demo or a game. They still cannot hear what
they made. They cannot tell a premium key press from a cheap one, notice that a hit lands 80 ms after the cut, or
hear that the music swells in the wrong place.

earshot turns sound into evidence an agent can reason about: what a file sounds like in words, how well it fits a
description, the best moment inside a long recording, whether it is a real recording or code-synthesized, a
second-by-second listening transcript of a whole film, an annotated picture of it, and a scorecard against
professional launch films. It runs locally on CPU, as a CLI, a Python API and an MCP server.

With ears, an agent can also **make its own sounds in code** and improve them by listening (`earshot forge`), and
**translate a recording into code** it can vary (`earshot fit`). Both below.

**New in 0.3: sound for code-made films.** A bank of 201 sound effects stored as code that render by id in seconds,
with no models and no network: `earshot sfx` aims a whoosh, hit, click or note at a moment in the picture, and
`earshot kit` renders a whole film's effects with measured sync points ([below](#sound-for-films-bank-sfx-kits)).

```
$ earshot describe enter.ogg
  0.56 s short transient (attack 3 ms, decays in 190 ms). Sounds most like: a single mechanical keyboard key press
  (z +5.4), a soft key release click (z +3.6) ... [clear reading]. peak -0.1 dBFS, brightness 1.5 kHz ...

$ earshot match key.ogg "a deep thocky mechanical keyboard press" --alts "a clicky blue switch keyboard" "a mouse click"
  -> strong (z +3.7; would rank #2 among 322 vocabulary descriptions) ...

$ earshot find keys.ogg "a single mechanical key press" --top 4
  0:03.94-0:04.19 (0.24 s stroke, z +4.1 strong); 0:10.60-0:10.86 ...

$ earshot critique film.mp4
  VERDICT: close - 21 of 23 scored metrics in range ... FIX FIRST: 1. [major] nothing reaches body level until 0:01.01 ...
```

## What it does

| command | what an agent gets |
|---|---|
| `describe FILE` | what it sounds like: calibrated tags (z) with the closest alternative readings, AudioSet labels, measurements |
| `match FILE QUERY [--alts ...]` | how well a description fits: cosine, z among the vocabulary, a verdict (strong / plausible / weak / no match) with held-out evidence |
| `rank QUERY PATHS...` | many candidate files sorted by a description (pick the best download) |
| `find FILE QUERY` | the best moments inside a long recording, as sample trims (start / end seconds) |
| `compare FILE --refs DIR` / `ab A B` | nearest reference recordings and typicality; A/B two sounds or two trims, the differences in words |
| `realness FILE...` | real recording / pro-produced vs code-synthesized, with evidence and per-window scores |
| `timeline FILE [--video V] [--cues C]` | the listening transcript: events (time, level, tag), sections, loudness, beat grid, sync of sound to picture cuts and cue frames |
| `sheet FILE -o out.png` | an annotated PNG (video frames, sections, labelled events, spectrogram, waveform, loudness, sync markers) for agents that read images |
| `critique FILE [--video V]` | a launch-video scorecard against a profile of 7 professional launch films, with timestamped fixes |
| `profile REFS... -o p.json` | build your own reference profile from films you admire |
| `measure FILE` | objective measurements only (no models): LUFS, true peak, LRA, envelope, spectrum, tempo / key |
| `forge RECIPE --refset CAT` | make a sound in code and improve it by listening (see below) |
| `fit FILE -o recipe.py` | translate a recording into a forge recipe module that re-renders it, with knobs and morphs (see below) |
| `sfx render ID -o x.wav` | a sound from the shipped bank of 201, aimed at the picture (`--dur`, `--apex`, `--pitch`) and audited; `sfx list`, `sfx check` (no models) |
| `kit init / render / check` | a film's sound kit: one bank sound per role, rendered into cached takes with measured onset / peak / end (no models) |
| `gallery DIR -o page.html` | one static HTML listening page of forge outputs: players, spectrograms, numbers |
| `llm FILE --yes-upload` | optional audio-LLM critique (Gemini), only with your own key and explicit consent |
| `mcp` | the same tools as an MCP server for Claude Code and other agents |
| `doctor [--load]` | check the install, models, data files and CPU settings |

Every command prints a plain-language summary first; `--json` gives the full result, `--out f.json` saves it. Errors

net-merge

Use all your internet connections at the same time.
Combine Wi-Fi, Ethernet and phone hotspots, so downloads, games and browsers get the speed of every connection added up.

Download · Install · Add a second connection · Troubleshooting · How it works


A Mac with Wi-Fi + an Android phone. The menu shows both connections working at once. Watch the full 45-second video.

net-merge uses all your network adapters together. It works on **Windows, macOS and Linux**. It is free. There is no account, no server and no VPN. A real test with Wi-Fi + an Android USB tether + an iPhone hotspot, 9 downloads at once: **232-303 Mbit/s**. The fastest connection alone gave about 121 Mbit/s. | Windows: hover the icon | Windows: the menu | macOS: the menu bar | |---|---|---| | ![Tooltip: Merging, speed of each adapter and the total](docs/tray-tooltip.png) | ![Menu: total, each adapter's speed and flows, IPv6 option, Pause merging, Quit](docs/tray-menu.png) | ![macOS menu: total 399 Mbit/s, en0 and feth0 each with their flows, Pause merging, Quit](docs/tray-menu-macos.png) | ## How it helps net-merge gives every new connection to one of your links. When an app opens many connections, they spread over all your links. - **Good for:** Steam and game downloads, browsers, system updates, cloud uploads (Google Drive), download managers like IDM, torrents. - **Not for:** one single connection. One connection always uses one link, so one big file from one connection does not get faster. - **Works for every app**, TCP and UDP, IPv4 and IPv6. You do not set up a proxy. - **Smart:** faster links get more connections. A link with no internet gets none until it works again. - **Safe:** if net-merge crashes, your internet keeps working. - **Light:** about 0.18 CPU cores per 100 Mbit/s. ## Install **macOS and Linux**: paste this into a terminal. ``` curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rohit267/net-merge/main/install.sh | sh ``` **Windows**: paste this into PowerShell. ``` irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rohit267/net-merge/main/install.ps1 | iex ``` That's it: net-merge is installed and its icon appears in the menu bar or tray. On Linux the script uses your package manager (apt, dnf, zypper, apk or pacman) and on macOS Homebrew when you have it, so net-merge updates with the rest of your system. To start it at sign-in: `net-merge autostart on`.
Rather type the commands yourself? One block per system, each ready to paste.
**Homebrew** (macOS): ``` brew install rohit267/tap/net-merge && sudo "$(brew --prefix)/bin/net-merge" install && net-merge tray ``` **macOS without Homebrew**: ``` curl -fsSL https://github.com/rohit267/net-merge/releases/latest/download/net-merge-macos-universal.tar.gz | tar -xz -C /tmp net-merge && sudo /tmp/net-merge install && net-merge tray ``` **Debian, Ubuntu, Linux Mint, Pop!_OS, Raspberry Pi OS** (apt): ``` curl -fsSL https://rohit267.github.io/net-merge/apt/key.gpg | sudo tee /usr/share/keyrings/net-merge.gpg >/dev/null echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/net-merge.gpg] https://rohit267.github.io/net-merge/apt stable main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/net-merge.list sudo apt update && sudo apt i

trend_summary: Недельная подборка из наблюдений GitHub Trending и поиска каждые три часа. Сначала проекты из недельного Trending, затем дневного, затем найденные новые репозитории. Для Trending показан максимальный наблюдавшийся +N своего периода, а не сумма срезов и не измеренный прирост за календарную неделю. Это ограниченная выборка, не рейтинг качества всего GitHub и не список новых релизов.
